I hope they start taking OS updates and fragmentation seriously. Honestly, the android ecosystem is a disaster today, with each vendor pushing their own flavor and older phones no longer getting security updates. Our mobile software team that builds apps for Android and iOS need to test on a few hundred phones before they can release something. The last count I saw was something like 1,200 phones out of which they covered about 40%.

This is only set to get worse, with more and more players entering the low to mid price Android handset market, you're expected to throw away your phone every 2 years. While the market is booming today, it's unsustainable in the long run.

I appreciate the way Apple controls the OS upgrade rollouts, and microsoft's plans for Win10 on the phones.

Whenever I use someone's iPhone, I'm always shocked at how good the apps are on iOS compared to Android. Everything is more polished, better designed, and there are significantly less bugs compared to Android. This isn't solely Google's fault. As you pointed out, every OEM needs to skin Android to differentiate from the rest of the market. If stock Android was the norm, there would probably be significantly less problems with apps compared to now.

It used to be that buying an Android phone was the only option, but as fragmentation and Google's tendency to put out half baked software Windows 10 and iOS are harder to not pick. I'm going to seriously look at the competition the next time I buy a phone.
